lines.text: In nineteen seventy-four, a team went to the World Cup... and never lost a single game. And still — they were sent home.
Perfection, punished by arithmetic. The cruellest exit in football history. And tonight, that ghost has come back.
Last time, we predicted the United States would edge Australia, two to one.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends, episode thirty-three. Scotland... versus Morocco.
The Tartan Army, against the Atlas Lions. And stay with me — because both nations have touched greatness, and felt it slip away.
Two stories of glorious heartbreak. Tonight, they collide.
First, the history. And it is true. West Germany, nineteen seventy-four.
Scotland drew with the mighty Brazil. They beat Zaire. They did not lose a single match.
And still they flew home — the first team ever knocked out of a World Cup without losing a game.
Out by a single goal. Unbeaten... and eliminated. The most heartbreaking exit the game has ever seen.
Fifty years on, the Tartan Army still dreams of laying that ghost to rest.
Now cross the water, to Morocco. Twenty twenty-two. A night that stopped a continent.
They knocked out Spain on penalties. They beat Portugal.
The first African nation ever to reach a World Cup semifinal.
Fourth in the world — the greatest run African football has ever seen.
So close to immortality they could taste it. Two proud nations, one shared, painful lesson.
Now, Scotland. Scott McTominay — the midfielder nobody believed in, who scores from nowhere.
Andy Robertson, the captain. Kieran Tierney, the warrior. John McGinn, twenty goals from midfield. Lawrence Shankland up top.
Highland fire — and a refusal, ever, to break.
And across from them — Morocco. Achraf Hakimi flies down the right. Hakim Ziyech bends magic with his left foot.
Youssef En-Nesyri climbs above everyone. Sofyan Amrabat runs forever. And young Bilal El-Khannouss pulls the strings.
So here is the duel. Highland fire... against the desert wind that swept aside the giants of Europe.
Our prediction — built on two stubborn defences, and two goalkeepers who decided this would be their night. Watch.
The thirty-third minute. Robertson swings the corner, and McTominay rises.
But the Moroccan keeper throws himself across — and palms it over. An impossible save. Still, nil-nil.
Then Morocco strike back. Ziyech whips it in, and En-Nesyri towers above the defence.
And the Scottish keeper flies through the air... and somehow keeps it out.
Nil-nil at the whistle, in our story. No goals — and two saves nobody will ever forget.
Do you agree? Comment SCOTLAND if the Tartan Army hold firm. Comment MOROCCO if the Atlas Lions break through.
And that ghost in the stands? Legend number thirty-three: the Ghost of Goal Difference.
He haunts every team that did everything right... and still went home. Tonight he came to see if heartbreak finally turns to glory. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to you. At WorldCup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score, scores for you.
Free to play, no prizes. Like, share, subscribe — the legends are only beginning.
